Tenure-track: Biological/Chemical Basis of Urban Environmental Health

Job Details

Position Description:

The Department of Natural Sciences invites applications for a full-time, tenure-track Assistant Professor position beginning in the 2027-2028 academic year at Fordham University Lincoln Center campus. We seek an innovative scholar whose research leverages unique opportunities to understand how aspects of urban environments interact with biological processes to impact health outcomes. Applicants must hold a Ph.D. in Biology, Chemistry, Environmental Science, or a closely related discipline and demonstrate a strong, proven excellence in undergraduate teaching and student mentoring. 

 

Priority will be given to candidates who conduct laboratory or field research relevant to New York City and its communities, and who maintain a strong research record of engaging undergraduate students in active research. Tenure-track faculty are expected to teach undergraduate lectures and laboratory courses across the Natural Sciences curriculum, and to develop new coursework at the intersection of urban environmental science and public health.

 

Qualifications

Ph.D. in Biology, Chemistry, Environmental Science, or a closely related discipline and demonstrate a strong, proven excellence in undergraduate teaching and student mentoring.

 

Application Instructions

All application materials must be submitted electronically Through Interfolio at this link: https://apply.interfolio.com/193415. Please review the position announcement carefully, including the required qualifications, application materials, and submission deadline.

 

Applicants should upload all materials identified below.

  • Curriculum vitae
  • Research statement
  • Teaching statement or teaching philosophy
  • Confidential recommendations (3)

 

Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until December 4th 2026. 

 

Equal Employment Opportunity Statement

Fordham University is committed to excellence through diversity and welcomes candidates of all backgrounds.

 

Fordham University is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, orientation, gender identity or expression, pregnancy, age, national origin, disability status, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

 

Effective October 24, 2025, the University will not approve or move forward with any new faculty hires that require the filing of an H-1B petition who are foreign nationals residing outside the U.S.  For all other aspects, we will continue to follow Fordham’s policy on Appointment of Nonimmigrant Faculty.
